Use the `--workers` option with the `fastapi` or `uvicorn` command. When deploying applications you will probably want to have some **replication of processes** to take advantage of **multiple cores** and to be able to handle more requests.[3]

**With the `fastapi` command:**

```console
$ fastapi run --workers 4 main.py
```

**With `uvicorn` directly:**

```console
$ uv run uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --workers 4
```

The only new option here is `--workers` telling Uvicorn to start 4 worker processes.[4] The output shows the **PID** of each process, `27365` for the parent process (this is the **process manager**) and one for each worker process[4].

**Using containers:** If you deploy on a cluster such as Kubernetes, you would not want to have multiple workers in the container, for example with the `--workers` command line option.[5] Instead, You would want to have just a **single Uvicorn process** per container (but probably multiple containers).[5] There are exceptions. One is when you deploy to a **single server** (not a cluster) with **Docker Compose**[5]. In that case you can set workers in the Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
CMD ["fastapi", "run", "app/main.py", "--port", "80", "--workers", "4"]
```

The docs I found don't say how many workers to use per CPU core. For more detail, see the "Server Workers" and "FastAPI in Containers - Docker" deployment pages.
